Change is sound and mechanically correct; I traced the factory paths to confirm.

What I verified in `src/maasserver/testing/factory.py`:
- `make_RackController(subnet=...)` → `make_Controller` → `make_Node_with_Interface_on_Subnet(interface_count=1, with_dhcp_rack_primary=False, with_dhcp_rack_secondary=False)` (lines 666-679). With `subnet` passed, `vlan = subnet.vlan` and no extra random subnet is created, so the rack ends up with exactly one interface on the test's `10.0.0.0/8` subnet. `rack.current_config.interface_set.first()` is therefore unambiguous.
- The `maasserver_discovery` view joins `subnet` on `vlan.id = subnet.vlan_id AND neigh.ip << subnet.cidr` ordered by `masklen DESC` (initial.maas_test.sql:5292). Old `test_associates_known_subnet` relied on `make_Subnet(..., vlan=iface.vlan)` while the rack's auto subnet lived on a different VLAN; the new form removes the second subnet entirely, which is strictly more deterministic. Also note `Subnet.cidr` is globally `unique=True` (models/subnet.py:347), so eliminating the extra random subnet removes the unique-cidr collision risk the description refers to.
- `by_unknown_ip()` filters purely on `StaticIPAddress.ip` (models/discovery.py:57-67), so swapping `cidr="10.0.0.0/8"` for `subnet=subnet` doesn't change what the assertions exercise — it just stops `make_StaticIPAddress` from implicitly creating/looking up a subnet on a fresh VLAN.

No bugs or security concerns found. Two optional cleanups below (explicit `boot_interface`, de-duplicated setup). Note that the untouched tests that keep `factory.make_Interface(node=rack)` (`test_query_by_unknown_mac`, `test_does_not_fail_if_cannot_find_subnet`) are correctly left alone: `make_Interface` with `vlan=None`/`subnet=None` builds a fresh fabric + default VLAN with no subnets (factory.py:1851-1869), which is exactly what the "cannot find subnet" assertion needs.

I could not execute `bin/test.region` in this review environment, so the verification above is static (factory/view source reading), not a test run.

src/maasserver/models/tests/test_discove.44: Optional: `rack.boot_interface` is more explicit than `current_config.interface_set.first()`. `make_Node_with_Interface_on_Subnet` assigns `node.boot_interface = boot_interface` (factory.py:1169-1173), whereas `.first()` is only well-defined here because `interface_count=1`; `Interface.Meta.ordering = ("created",)` (models/interface.py:541) would make it ambiguous if a second interface were ever added to the fixture. That said, `interface_set.first()` is the dominant convention in these two files, so keeping it is defensible — just don't add a second interface later without switching.
src/maasserver/models/tests/test_discove.42:
The 3-line setup (`make_Subnet` / `make_RackController(subnet=...)` / grab iface) is now repeated 4x across this file and `api/tests/test_discoveries.py`. A small module-level helper returning `(subnet, iface)` would cut the duplication and make the intent ("rack interface on a known subnet") self-documenting, per the repo's "suggest refactoring when code duplication is detected" guideline.

Minor, pre-existing: `make_Subnet(cidr="10.0.0.0/8")` defaults `gateway_ip` to `first + 1` = `10.0.0.1` (factory.py:1555-1557), i.e. the same address these tests use as the discovered IP. Harmless for the current assertions, but `gateway_ip=None` would decouple the fixture from that coincidence.
src/maasserver/models/tests/test_discove.75: Nothing to change here — just confirming the scoping: this test still uses `make_Interface(node=rack)`, which creates a brand-new fabric and default VLAN with no subnets (factory.py:1851-1869), so the view's `vlan.id = subnet.vlan_id` join can never match and `subnet is None` stays deterministic. Applying the new pattern here would break the test's premise.

src/maasserver/api/tests/test_discoverie.130: Same setup block as `models/tests/test_discovery.py:42-44`; if you extract a helper there, consider putting it somewhere both modules can use (or just accept the duplication — this file already repeats `make_RackController()` + `interface_set.first()` ~15 times, so the pattern is consistent with the surrounding code).
